title: IT stocks couldn’t save Nifty as crude, Fed fears drag markets into red - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Markets reversed their morning gains by midday on Tuesday, with the Nifty 50 sliding 81.05 points (0.35 per cent) to 23,317.05 and the Sensex falling 134.29 points (0.18 per cent) to 74,647.47 as of 12.31 pm, as selling pressure across financials, industrials and consumer stocks overwhelmed a strong rally in information technology shares.

The Sensex had opened the session at 75,369.63 against a previous close of 74,781.76, while the Nifty opened at 23,576.15 against a previous close of 23,398.10, both indices gapping up before retreating sharply through the morning session.

Information technology stocks continued to dominate the gainers list, extending the morning’s sector rotation. HCL Technologies led the Nifty 50 with a gain of 5.68 per cent to ₹1,274.60 on volumes of 32.81 lakh shares worth ₹41,969.97 lakhs. TCS rose 4.76 per cent to ₹2,305.50, with 37 lakh shares traded valued at ₹85,295.06 lakhs, the highest value traded among all gainers. Infosys gained 3.95 per cent to ₹1,078.70 on exceptional volumes of over 1.04 crore shares worth ₹1,13,084.65 lakhs. Tech Mahindra added 3.70 per cent to ₹1,598.00, and TMPV rose 2.64 per cent to ₹309.05.

...”The IT sector emerged as the standout performer, rising more than 4.5 per cent in early trade as investors rotated toward Indian software companies with established, traditional business models following the sharp sell-off in global technology stocks,”... said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. The rotation came after senior AI executives publicly raised concerns over the pace of AI development, prompting a global reassessment of high-valuation technology stocks.

Losses were spread across multiple sectors. Shriram Finance fell 3.57 per cent to ₹991.90 on volumes of 32.59 lakh shares worth ₹32,773.77 lakhs, while BEL declined an equal 3.57 per cent to ₹389.90 with over 1 crore shares traded worth ₹39,449.28 lakhs. Grasim dropped 2.71 per cent to ₹3,192.80, Adani Enterprises fell 2.38 per cent to ₹2,987.30, and Titan lost 2.25 per cent to ₹4,897.00.

Broad market breadth on the BSE confirmed the negative tone: of 4,513 stocks traded, 2,884 declined against 1,376 advances and 253 unchanged. There were 263 stocks in the lower circuit versus 181 in the upper circuit. The number of stocks at 52-week lows, at 156, nearly matched those at 52-week highs at 151.

Brent crude trading near $107 a barrel and WTI at $102.82, up 0.92 per cent on the day, remained the dominant macro concern. A fresh report of an attack on Strait of Hormuz shipping added to the geopolitical risk premium in oil markets, with WTI’s RSI at 71, firmly in overbought territory. MCX Crude Oil opened with a gap up, trading above ₹9,800, up 1.38 per cent, with immediate resistance at the psychological ₹10,000 mark.

...”Elevated crude prices remain a key concern for India, as a prolonged period of higher oil prices could widen the import bill, add to inflationary pressures and weigh on corporate margins,”... said Ponmudi R. Domestic data reinforced this concern: India’s consumer price inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July.

The USD/INR pair extended its recent move, testing the 95.80 resistance zone after the rupee weakened more than 1 per cent last week to close near 95.55. A sustained break above 95.80 could open the path toward 96.00–96.10. The RSI on the pair at 61 confirmed strong bullish momentum in the dollar. ...”The rupee remains under pressure from elevated crude oil prices, firm dollar demand and rising Treasury yields, with the Fed’s two-day meeting now in focus for the next directional cue,”... noted Ponmudi R.

COMEX Gold tested the $4,340–4,300 support zone, nearly flat on the day, with its RSI at 44 confirming soft momentum. MCX Gold held above the ₹1,50,700–1,50,000 support zone, up marginally at 0.09 per cent, with immediate resistance at ₹1,54,000. COMEX Silver edged lower, down 0.25 per cent, testing the $64.000–63.500 support zone, while MCX Silver fell 0.35 per cent, trading below the ₹2,33,000–2,34,000 resistance zone. ...”Gold continues to underperform expectations for a safe haven, weighed down by a stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields ahead of the Fed decision,”... Enrich Money’s technical commentary noted.

The Federal Reserve’s two-day FOMC meeting, which began today, remained the single most-watched event globally. Markets are pricing a 60 per cent probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike, driven by persistent energy-led inflation and strong U.S. consumer credit data, which came in at $18.06 billion against a forecast of $11.90 billion. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, which briefly crossed 5 per cent overnight, continued to reflect investor unease.

Technically, the Nifty’s gap-up open near 23,576 faced early rejection just below the crucial 23,600 resistance level. ...”The index will require a sustained and decisive breakout above the 23,600 zone to strengthen the recovery and pave the way towards the 23,800–24,000 levels,”... said Ponmudi R, adding that a decisive break below 23,200 could trigger fresh selling pressure. The RSI on the Nifty, while recovering from deeply oversold territory, still hovered around 32, indicating momentum remains weak.

Bank Nifty opened near 56,884 but faced selling pressure around the 57,000 psychological level. Immediate support remains at the 56,200–56,000 zone, and a breach below 56,000 could weaken the near-term structure further.
